sections.label: Common services tunnels Bill introduced
sections.summary: The Bill introduces legislation for safe and efficient operation of common services tunnels, with one existing CST at Marina Bay.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With this Bill, we are introducing new legislation to ensure the safe and efficient operation of common services tunnels (CSTs).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: A CST is an underground tunnel which houses multiple utilities to serve an area.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There is, currently, one CST in Singapore, located under the roads at Marina Bay.

sections.label: New CST Bill purposes
sections.summary: The new CST Bill makes arrangements clear in law, clarifies grey areas and enhances regulatory practices for safe CST operation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Drawing on our experiences with the Marina Bay CST, we are introducing this new CST Bill to make these arrangements clear in the law, to clarify any grey areas and enhance our regulatory practices to ensure the safe and efficient operation of CSTs.

sections.label: Utilities laid within CST
sections.summary: The Bill makes clear all utilities in the CST area are to be laid within the CST unless approval is given otherwise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, the Bill makes clear that all utilities in the CST area are to be laid within the CST, unless approval is given to do otherwise.

sections.label: Approval conditions and railway comparison
sections.summary: The Bill is similar to the railway protection zone, and officers may impose conditions to prevent damage to the CST.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is similar to the "railway protection zone" under the Rapid Transit Systems Act, which safeguards MRT tunnels against damage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is necessary as damage to the CST could cut off the power or water supply to buildings in these areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In issuing their approval, officers may impose conditions deemed necessary to prevent damage or adverse impact on the operation of the CST.

sections.label: Penalties for violations
sections.summary: The Bill sets maximum penalties of $20,000 and up to $1,000 a day for continuing offences, and jail for obstruction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Bill also sets out the maximum penalties for violations of these provisions which are set at $20,000 and up to $1,000 a day for continuing offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For obstructing officers in the course of duty, the penalty also includes a jail term of up to six months.

sections.label: Marina Bay CST infrastructure cost
sections.summary: The two phases of the Marina Bay CST had planning from as early as 1998, with base infrastructure cost over $330 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The high upfront infrastructure capital cost involved, as well as the time required to build such a structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am given to understand that the two phases of the Marina Bay CST (MBCST) had planning begin as early as 1998 and, coupled with the district cooling plant, base infrastructure cost has amounted to over $330 million so far.

sections.label: Bill formalises existing practices
sections.summary: The Bill's provisions mostly formalise practices already in place, after learning from Marina Bay's operational and regulatory experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As Mr Alex Yam noted, most of the provisions of the Bill serve to formalise practices which are already in place today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We had taken some time to learn from the experience in Marina Bay, the operational experience, the regulatory experience, before we decided to put together and codify all of these into the Bill that we have today.

sections.label: Potential CST sites studied
sections.summary: CSTs show potential in Jurong Lake District and Changi Airport Terminal 5, but detailed cost-benefit studies are still needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Preliminarily, we see potential for CSTs in newer developments like Jurong Lake District and Changi Airport Terminal 5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But more detailed studies will be needed to determine the cost-benefits of such a project.
